questions.q: What is Structured Streaming's core conceptual model?
options: Treating a continuously arriving data source as an unbounded table that keeps growing, one micro-batch at a time
A completely separate API unrelated to DataFrames
A way to convert streaming data into a fixed-size batch file
Only usable with SQL, never the DataFrame API
questions.explain: This is the exact same DataFrame concept from Foundations' Chapter 4, just fed continuously instead of once.

questions.q: What's the main structural difference between spark.read and spark.readStream?
options: That's structurally almost the whole difference — most DataFrame methods like .filter() work exactly the same on either
readStream requires an entirely different set of transformation methods
readStream can only be used with CSV files
readStream doesn't support .filter() or .select() at all
questions.explain: Foundations Lesson 45's .filter() works exactly the same on a streaming DataFrame as a batch one.

questions.q: What does trigger(availableNow=True) let a streaming pipeline do that processingTime doesn't?
options: Process everything currently available, once, then stop — fitting neatly into a scheduled job rather than running indefinitely
Run continuously forever, checking on a fixed interval
Skip the checkpoint requirement entirely
Process data faster than processingTime in every case
questions.explain: This is the same trigger style Lesson 32's Autoloader used, making it fit a scheduled job (Lesson 11).

questions.q: What genuinely new concepts does streaming add on top of the DataFrame API already covered in Foundations?
options: The checkpoint (tracking progress across restarts) and the trigger (how often to check) — the only real additions
An entirely new set of column functions unrelated to pyspark.sql.functions
A requirement to abandon select/filter/groupBy entirely
Nothing; streaming requires learning a completely separate system
questions.explain: Everything else — select, filter, withColumn, groupBy — works essentially unchanged on a streaming DataFrame.

options: A small batch of new rows processed at each trigger interval
A single row processed in isolation
A synonym for a Delta table's checkpoint file
A batch job that reprocesses the entire table from scratch
questions.explain: This is the underlying mechanism behind the "unbounded table" idea — growing one micro-batch at a time.
